payload.question_text: A marketing team is choosing metrics for AI-written product descriptions. It needs qualitative evidence of factual support, writing clarity, and similarity to an approved reference style. Which choices best fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Groundedness provides qualitative evidence about factual support. It addresses whether claims are supported.
F1 is a classic NLP metric. By itself it does not provide the requested qualitative evidence.
options.better_fit: Use F1 when a traditional quantitative metric is specifically needed.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would miss the required qualitative review.
feedback.instructional: Use AI-assisted metrics for qualitative qualities beyond F1.

options.rationale: Coherence and fluency assess clarity and flow of writing. They address the writing-quality criterion.
GPT similarity is an AI-assisted quality metric. It fits comparison with an approved reference style.

payload.explanation: Correct. These metrics address the stated quality dimensions.

payload.question_text: A support manager must choose between a catalog model, an agent action, and a prebuilt Foundry capability for a single standardized workflow. Fast time-to-value and built-in compliance matter most. Which decision is best?

options.rationale: Catalog selection is useful when choosing among model capabilities. It adds selection work when a prebuilt solution fits.
options.better_fit: Select a catalog model when the use case requires a tailored choice among model capabilities.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would take on extra selection work.
feedback.instructional: For a fixed workflow, a Foundry tool is the closer fit.

options.rationale: The workflow is standardized, and speed and compliance are priorities. A Foundry tool uses prebuilt models for this need.
Agent actions let an agent call external capabilities. They are not the prebuilt solution described.
options.better_fit: Use an agent action when an agent must call an API or retrieve external information.

feedback.intrinsic: An action alone would not deliver the standardized solution.
feedback.instructional: This decision concerns a prebuilt Foundry capability, not an agent integration.

options.rationale: A leaderboard helps rank models. It does not provide the requested workflow solution.
options.better_fit: Open a leaderboard when comparing model attributes before selection.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would have rankings but no direct solution.
feedback.instructional: A Foundry tool is intended for the defined workflow.

payload.explanation: Correct. The criteria favor a Foundry tool.

metadata.unit_title: Compare, score, and deploy models · Level 3
metadata.unit_slo: Evaluate model outputs and explain what happens when a model is deployed.

evaluation_context.goal: Produce an excellent, source-faithful learner session while preserving all deterministic correctness, identity, and sequence constraints.
evaluation_context.source_fidelity_goal: Independently verify the hard-gated edited challenger against the supplied source material. Reject unsupported facts, answers, explanations, feedback, or terminology changes; do not edit the artifact.

criteria.factual_fidelity: Every claim and answer is faithful to the supplied source.
criteria.answer_unambiguity: Each item has one defensible answer under its instructions.
criteria.distractor_plausibility: Distractors are credible without becoming defensible answers.
criteria.misconception_quality: Wrong choices diagnose realistic learner misconceptions.
criteria.cognitive_progression: The ordered session builds understanding at a coherent pace.
criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.
criteria.scenario_authenticity: Scenarios resemble credible decisions or tasks.
criteria.feedback_usefulness: Feedback explains the governing concept and next step.
criteria.difficulty_appropriateness: Difficulty matches the stated audience and session position.
criteria.terminology_consistency: Terms are used consistently with the source and across items.
criteria.overall_learner_experience: The exact final sequence is coherent, varied, and instructive.
